# FDG9138

> DO use `ReadOnlySpan<T>` instead of `Span<T>` where possible.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.12 Operating on Buffers.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG9138
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Declare the parameter '{0}' of '{1}' as ReadOnlySpan&lt;{2}>; the method only reads it

FDG9138 reports a Span&lt;T> parameter passed by value to an externally visible method or constructor with a body when the body only reads it: every use is its Length or IsEmpty, an element read through the indexer, a conversion to ReadOnlySpan&lt;T> (passing it to a ReadOnlySpan&lt;T> parameter included), CopyTo, TryCopyTo, ToArray or ToString called on it, a read-only MemoryExtensions method called on it (Contains, IndexOf, LastIndexOf, IndexOfAny, LastIndexOfAny, SequenceEqual, SequenceCompareTo, StartsWith, EndsWith or BinarySearch), a foreach without ref, or nameof; a parameter that is not used at all is reported too. Any other use counts as a possible write and the parameter is not reported: assigning or incrementing an element or assigning the parameter, passing it as Span&lt;T>, passing an element by reference or binding it to a ref local, an element as the target of a deconstruction assignment (a tuple swap), Slice, a range, and a member access on an element when T is not a reference type. So coverage is partial. Virtual, abstract and extern methods, overrides and interface implementations are not reported, since their parameter types are a contract for other implementations. A method whose body only throws (an expression body => throw, or a block whose only statement is a throw) is not reported: ReadOnlySpan&lt;T> is not possible, as the text puts it, for a stub such as a PlatformNotSupportedException method that keeps the Span&lt;T> signature of the implementation on other targets; this also hides throw-only methods that could take ReadOnlySpan&lt;T>. The book's Sum(Span&lt;int> values) is reported. Span&lt;T> and Memory&lt;T> types need .NET Core 2.1 or later, or the System.Memory package on .NET Framework and .NET Standard 2.0 (see FDG9137). Changing the parameter type changes the public signature, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

The `System.ReadOnlySpan<T>` type does not support value mutation. When a method accepts a `ReadOnlySpan<T>` instead of a `Span<T>`, it provides a signal to the caller that the called method will not be replacing the contents of the span. Accepting a `ReadOnlySpan<T>` when possible also allows more callers to the method, because all `Span<T>` values can be freely converted to `ReadOnlySpan<T>`, but `ReadOnlySpan<T>` values cannot be converted back to `Span<T>`.

`String` values logically represent an immutable `char[]`, and can be converted to `ReadOnlySpan<char>`, but not `Span<char>`.

```csharp
public static long Sum(ReadOnlySpan<int> values) {
    long sum = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < values.Length; i++) {
        sum += values[i];
    }
    return sum;
}

// Good: An array overload, either an existing method
// or one added concurrently
public static long Sum(int[] values) {
    if (values == null) {
        throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(values));
    }
    return Sum(values.AsSpan());
}

// Bad: This method suggests it writes to the parameter, but it only
// reads. Writable spans are freely convertible to ReadOnlySpan.
public static long Sum(Span<int> values) {
    return Sum((ReadOnlySpan<int>)values);
}
```
